the_two_defects.precise_description: a host-resident statistics snapshot missing its compute-device working copy. NOT a mutation of the persistent StatsCache policy: `AttentionHeadStatsCollector.state()` returns host-resident tensors BY DESIGN — that is the evidence and cache form — and the operator passed that snapshot directly into `head_write_energy`, where it met `o_proj.weight` on cuda:0.
the_two_defects.observed_as: RuntimeError: Expected all tensors to be on the same device, but found at least two devices, cuda:0 and cpu! at src/aadistill/init/attention_stats.py:146
the_two_defects.repair: host_stats = collector.state(); collector.release(); stats = stats_to(host_stats, compute). Exactly one per-invocation working copy on model_device(parent), built with the existing aadistill.autoinit.device.stats_to.
explicitly_not_done: model weights were NOT moved to CPU
the persistent cache was NOT made CUDA-resident
no new cache abstraction was introduced
head_write_energy was NOT taught to guess or transfer silently
the_two_defects.release_rationale: state() copies the (layers, heads, d, d) float64 accumulator to the host; without release() the device original, the host snapshot and the new working copy are all alive at once. release() frees the collector's device accumulator between the snapshot and the working copy, so at most two exist. state() after release() raises rather than returning a stale or absent accumulator.

the_two_defects.precise_description: a fresh factory with no placement. `scores = torch.empty(num_heads, dtype=torch.float64)` defaults to CPU, so on a GPU the first `scores[h] = ...` store is a second cross-device use — latent behind defect 1 and unreachable until it was fixed.
the_two_defects.repair: placement is derived from the tensor the vector meets: `device=w.device`. All scores are computed on the compute device and the small (num_heads,) vector is moved to the host exactly once, after it is built, because every caller ranks, sums and tie-breaks on the host.
the_two_defects.fail_closed: head_write_energy now raises when m.device != w.device instead of transferring. A silent repair there would make the function guess which device the caller meant and would hide a caller that forgot its working copy; the co-location is the CALLER's contract, and the error names aadistill.autoinit.device.stats_to as the remedy.
